item.title: 2026 Mulan International Film Festival — Sun Nov 22, 3:00 PM — Innis Town Hall
item.description:
From November 21 to December 3, join the 7th Mulan International Film Festival at Toronto’s Innis Town Hall. As the largest film festival dedicated to Chinese-language cinema in North America, Mulan brings restored classics and new voices to the big screen.
Opening night presents the Canadian premiere of the 4K restoration of Patrick TAM’s Love Massacre, starring Brigitte LIN. The festival closes with the North American premiere of CHONG Keat Aun’s Golden Horse Award-winning Mother Bhumi, winner of Best Leading Actress for FAN Bingbing, Best Cinematography and Best Original Film Song.
Discover six features and nine shorts from emerging filmmakers in the Fountainhead competition programme, and vote for your favourites. Other highlights include the world premiere of the new 4K restoration of Clara LAW’s Farewell, China, starring Maggie CHEUNG and Tony LEUNG Ka-Fai, and On Canvas, On Stage, a complete retrospective of QIU Jiongjiong’s films, including A New Old Play and Madame.

York University’s Koschitzky Centre for Jewish Studies and the Department of Music in the School of the Arts, Media, Performance and Design invite you to the opening of the fifth season of Sound and Sense: Jewish Music at York, with a special release concert celebrating Pursue Peace, the initiative’s debut album. The program brings together the work of three distinguished Canadian composers and leading performers in an evening of music shaped by memory, identity, history, and the many ways music gives voice to human experience.

item.title: Fetish: The Science of What Turns Us On — Mon Nov 23, 7:00 AM — Come As You Are
item.description:
Overview How does something ordinary become intensely erotic—and what can our most unusual turn-ons teach us about desire? Join sex educator and author Niki Davis-Fainbloom for a playful, research-backed workshop inspired by her new book, Fetish: Smash Taboos and Celebrate What Turns You On. Drawing on hundreds of studies, interviews, and an original survey of 260 people, Niki explores how biology, conditioning, and culture shape our erotic imaginations. Along the way, you’ll meet some of the book’s fascinating characters, including a woman whose love of bicycles shaped her romantic life and a man who enjoys being wrapped in carpet and stepped on. Through storytelling, guided reflection, interactive discussions, and a science-backed Q&A, we’ll explore where desires come from, why certain fantasies stick, and how to approach our turn-ons with curiosity and less shame. Expect surprising science, practical communication tools, and plenty of room for questions.
Source: blogTO

Join Chess master Jennifer Shahade, author of Thinking Sideways and Chess Queens, and Star Opinion Editor Jordan Himelfarb, author of his own book on chess, for an interactive conversation about strategy, decision-making and how to see the board differently when the obvious move fails. Drawing on chess, poker, gender and power, this event will invite audiences to think in moves, countermoves and possibilities — and to ask what changes when we stop looking for the right answer and start looking for the better move. About Toronto Star Live at Soulpepper: Bringing journalism to the stage. In partnership with the Toronto Star, this new monthly series transforms the theatre into a public forum for the city, a place where journalists, guest speakers, and audiences come together to examine the ideas shaping Toronto right now. Tickets are $40 and doors open at 6:30PM

item.title: Out of Line: 150 Years of Supporting Creative Defiance at OCAD U — Tue Nov 24, 6:00 PM — Ignite Gallery
item.description:
This exhibition is free to attend. The Student Galleries mark OCAD University’s 150th anniversary with a pointed declaration of purpose by positioning the institution not merely as a site of technical training or aesthetic refinement, but rather as a long-standing incubator of creative disruption. Out of Line gathers notable alumni and long-time faculty whose practices embody this refusal. These artists do not form a school or style, but rather what binds them is a shared willingness to step across boundaries, to trouble conventions, and to keep culture unsettled in the interest of possibility. The exhibition is both celebration and summons—a recognition of what has been achieved and an invitation to keep the boundaries moving. This exhibition is free to attend.
Source: blogTO

item.description:
Growing native plants from seed is an inexpensive and easy way to add plants to your garden – but you need to start early! Many native plants require several months of cold temperatures to sprout in the spring. Join this session with Toronto Master Gardeners to learn where to get your seed and how to sow it over the winter for germination in the spring. At the end of the program, native seeds will be given out to attendees, while supplies last. Suitable for gardeners of any skill level, with any kind of outdoor space. This program is part of Toronto Public Library's Our Fragile Planet program series, supported by Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter.​ Registration required. item.title: Winterreise — Wed Nov 25, 8:00 PM — The Citadel: Ross Centre for Dance
item.description:
Citadel + Compagnie and Echo Chamber are proud to present the world premiere of Winterreise from November 25-28, 2026 for four performances at The Citadel: Ross Centre for Dance in Toronto. Reimagined for violin, piano, and tenor and soprano voices, this moving adaptation of Franz Schubert’s Winterreise intertwines live music and dance to explore love, loss, and the search for belonging in Schubert’s timeless song cycle. Winterreise tells the story of a solitary traveller wandering through a frozen world of memory and longing. This new adaptation from Citadel + Compagnie and Echo Chamber dives deeper into the traveller's past using delicate choreography and music with Wilhelm Müller’s words sung in English to allow the inherent poetry of the work to shine through.
Source: blogTO
